title: Ghost-RISB for Correlated Electron-Phonon Systems: Application to the Hubbard-Holstein Model
authors: Samuele Giuli, Ricardo J. Campos-Lopes, Emin Moghadas, Massimo Capone
abstract: We develop a generalization of the ghost-rotationally-invariant slave-boson (ghost-RISB) method that incorporates local phonon modes coupled to arbitrary on-site electronic degrees of freedom, enabling a nonperturbative treatment of electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions within an efficient variational framework. The method extends the ghost-orbital construction to capture dynamical self-energy effects and phonon-induced renormalizations beyond static slave-boson approaches. Benchmarking against dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) results for the Hubbard-Holstein model, we find excellent quantitative agreement for electron quasiparticle weights and phonon properties across a wide range of coupling strengths, and it captures accurately the competition between electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions. We show that the inclusion of the ghost orbitals is crucial to accurately describe the regime of low-frequency, strongly dynamical, phonons. The extended ghost-RISB achieves this accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost of DMFT, due to its self-consistency rooted in static observables instead of dynamical ones, enabling rapid exploration of correlated electron-phonon phase diagrams. We exploit this advantage to characterize the most demanding regime of strong coupling and adiabatic phonons. Our analysis shows a suppression of the superconducting order parameter, which is interpreted as a Franck-Condon-like reduction of the overlap between the phonon wavefunctions associated with empty and doubly-occupied sites in the bipolaronic regime.
summary: This paper introduces an advanced theoretical tool, the ghost-RISB method, to tackle the challenging physics of correlated electron-phonon interactions in models like Hubbard-Holstein. It successfully reproduces key results from computationally intensive DMFT while offering superior efficiency for mapping out complex phase diagrams, particularly concerning superconductivity suppression.
main_problem: The primary goal is developing a theoretical framework to accurately treat the complex interplay between electron-electron correlation (Hubbard repulsion) and local electron-phonon coupling in quantum materials.
main_result: The generalized ghost-RISB method achieves quantitative agreement with DMFT for key observables like quasiparticle weights, while being significantly more computationally efficient. It also predicts a suppression of the superconducting order parameter in the bipolaronic regime.
method: The authors generalize the ghost-rotationally-invariant slave-boson (ghost-RISB) method by incorporating local phonon modes into the variational framework. This involves mapping the problem onto an enlarged Fock space and solving saddle-point equations derived from a Lagrangian formulation.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the Hubbard-Holstein model, which describes fermions coupled to local optical phonon modes via terms for hopping ($t$), on-site repulsion ($U$), phonon energy ($\omega_0$), and electron-phonon coupling ($g$).
key_observables: Electron quasiparticle weights (Z), superconducting order parameter, and charge-resolved phonon distributions ($P_2(X)$ and $P_0(X)$).
important_parameters: Coupling strengths are characterized by dimensionless ratios like $\lambda = 2g^2/\omega_0$. The analysis covers regimes ranging from weak to strong coupling.
main_assumptions: The method relies on mean-field decoupling for both bosonic and fermionic fields, and the final results are obtained by imposing static saddle point conditions on the derived Lagrangian.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares DMFT results with ghost-RISB calculations for the quasi-particle weight Z under varying electron-electron coupling strengths (U).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the Hamiltonian, develops the generalized ghost-RISB formalism by mapping to an enlarged space and deriving a Lagrangian ($\mathcal{L}_{	ext{gRISB}}$), solves the resulting saddle point equations for matrix fields, benchmarks against DMFT, and finally applies the framework to analyze superconducting pairing in the bipolaronic regime.
why_interesting: The method provides a computationally cheaper alternative to DMFT for strongly coupled electron-phonon systems, allowing rapid phase diagram exploration that is critical for understanding materials like high-Tc superconductors or polaronic conductors.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: Figure 1: Effect of electron-phonon interaction on the quasi- particle weight Z measured by the ratio Z(λ)/Z(λ = 0) for ω0 = 0.2 and U = 0.5D (circles), U = 1.0D (squares), U = 1.5D (triangles) and U = 2.0D (diamond). The figure compares DMFT (black, dotted line) extracted from Ref. [29] with ghost-RISB using B = 5 (dark green, dash-dot line), B = 3 (green, dashed line) and B = 1 (light green, contin- uous line).

Figure 2: Mass renormalisation as a function of the phonon frequency for n = 0.9 (top panel), n = 0.7 (central panel) and n = 0.5 (bottom panel) at fixed U = 5D. In each panel, we plot B = 1 (light green, continuous line), B = 3 (green, dashed line) and B = 5 (dark green, dash-dot line), together with DMFT (dotted gray lines). The markers indicate λ = 1.0D (triangle), λ = 0.5D (diamond) and λ = 0.1D (circle). The agreement increases with doping and with the number of ghosts. B = 5 is in perfect agreement with DMFT data from Ref.[30].

Figure 3: Phonon probability distribution functions for dif- ferent values of λ. We compare the case of the half-filled Hol- stein model (upper panel) and the Hubbard-Holstein model at U/D = 1 (lower panel), both with a characteristic frequency of ω0/D = 0.2. The calculations are for B = 1 and B = 3 and are compared with DMFT data extracted from [69, 72].

Figure 4: Total and charge-resolved phonon probability dis- tribution functions projected to the empty, single, and double- occupied charge sectors. We compare the half-filled Holstein model (upper panel) at λ/D = 1.1 and the doped Hubbard- Holstein model at U/D = 5, λ/D = 2.2 (lower panel) at a filling of n = 0.7, both with a characteristic frequency of ω0/D = 0.2. The calculations are done for B = 3 and com- pared with DMFT data at the same parameter values.

Figure 5: Holstein model (U/D = 0 and ω0/D = 1.0) plot of (a) superconducting order parameter (black) and double- holon overlap Idh (red) for B = 1 (dots) and B = 3 (line) and as a function of the effective attraction λ. In green the area at which we identify the polaronic crossover. (b) Phononic dis- tribution function showed for values of λ/D between 0.0 (light gray) and 2.0 (black) passing through the polaronic crossover (green) around λ = 1.1 using B = 1 (dots) and B = 3 (line).
